summary: Two genuine Marketplace one-click routes (Hermes and OpenClaw) at the plan price, a documented guide for n8n, Discord bots and MCP servers, and a manual install for everything else. Vultr adds no picks: the one-click apps are cheaper elsewhere or ship a default password, and the always-on VPS case is already covered.

hermes-agent.what: The Marketplace HermesAgent app deploys Hermes on Ubuntu 24.04 with a Vultr Serverless Inference key you supply at launch, plus a web login. The listing prints a default password (hermes / Password) and channel setup is done in the app, so budget a first login and a password change.
hermes-agent.price: 2 vCPU / 4 GiB plan $20/mo; no app surcharge

openclaw.what: The Marketplace OpenClaw app deploys the gateway on Ubuntu 24.04 with Homebrew, Docker and a browser VS Code terminal, and a default clawmine / Password login. Change the password and treat the Code Server terminal as root-equivalent access.
openclaw.price: 2 vCPU / 4 GiB plan $20/mo; no app surcharge

coding-agent.what: Create a 4 vCPU / 8 GiB instance, SSH in and install Claude Code or Codex. Vultr's Codex guide uses Dokploy for the deploy half; the agent itself is a terminal install, and the disk survives a stop but the server bills through it.
coding-agent.price: $40/mo for 4 vCPU / 8 GiB, on or stopped

code-interpreter.what: There is no execution API or sandbox pool. You would build the run endpoint and machine pool on the Vultr API, and the one-hour minimum makes 20,000 one-minute runs cost 20,000 server-hours.

browser-agent.what: No browser or computer-use product. The Neko guide installs a virtual browser in Docker on a 4-core / 8 GB server; every ten-minute session still bills a whole hour, so 30,000 sessions are uneconomic.
browser-agent.price: $0.02976 per server-hour, one hour minimum per session

workflow-automation.what: Vultr's n8n guide runs n8n and Traefik from Docker Compose on Ubuntu 24.04, with the database and encryption key on the instance disk. It is a terminal build, not a Marketplace app.

chat-bot.what: Vultr's Discord guide deploys a Docker app and runs a Python bot inside it; keep it as a service and store the token on the disk. A gateway connection needs the machine awake, and Vultr has no idle stop.

claude-code-team.what: One instance per developer in a shared IAM organization, each with its own SSH key and Claude login. Five 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machines cost $200 a month whether the developers work eight hours or twenty-four.

scheduled-scraper.what: Run cron or a systemd timer inside an always-on instance, or create a fresh instance per run through the API. A fresh 1 vCPU / 2 GiB instance is billed a whole hour per run, so 120 ten-minute runs cost about $1.79 against $10 for an always-on box; write results to Object Storage.

mcp-server.what: Vultr's MCP guide runs a FastMCP server on an Ubuntu instance and reaches it over HTTP; add TLS and authentication yourself. The instance needs a public IPv4 and must stay up.

notPicked.reason: A real one-click app at $20/mo, but DigitalOcean and Hostinger already make the one-click Hermes case, and Vultr's listing prints a default password.
A one-click app at $20/mo, but DigitalOcean's hardened $12 image is cheaper and already a pick.
Manual install only; Vultr has no preinstalled coding agent.
